parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
In Senegal, 2% of the population are involved in coastal fishing.
Calculate the number of people in Senegal involved in coastal fishing in 2018.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Senegal has a rapidly increasing population.
Describe factors that cause changes in human population.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Explain why the proportion of the population of Senegal under the age of 25 is likely to
continue to increase.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
Only 30% of the crops grown in Senegal are consumed in the country.
Suggest what happens to the remaining 70% of crops grown in Senegal.

parts.label: (v)
parts.text:
Suggest reasons why it is a risk to the population of Senegal to rely on only 30% of the
country’s crops.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The photograph shows some young mango trees with mango fruits growing on a small farm.
The mango trees are planted in rows 10 m apart.
Suggest reasons why the farmer has planted the mango trees in this way.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The fact sheet shows some information about mango fruits.
Mango fruit fact sheet
• Mango fruits are an important part of the diet in Senegal
• 16 000 tonnes of mango fruits are exported from 2500 small farms
• fertilisers and pesticides are not used on small farms
• mango fruits are harvested between April and September
• the best quality mango fruits are exported from Senegal in July and August
• it is only possible to export mango fruits if they are grown 50 km or less
from the capital city, Dakar.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Calculate the average mass of mango fruits exported from each small farm.
______ tonnes

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The Casamance region of Senegal grows mango fruits.
Suggest reasons why farms in the Casamance region cannot export mango fruits.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
A local farmer said,
In September we always have to leave
some mango fruits on the trees. The fruits
fall off the trees and rot on the ground.
Explain how leaving the mango fruits to rot on the ground can help fruit production the
following year.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
Suggest one other reason why farmers leave some mango fruits on the trees in
September.

parts.text:

parts.text: Suggest one other question the student could have asked the mango farmers.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
The student concluded that most of the farms grow two local varieties of mango fruit.
To what extent do the results support this conclusion?

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text: Suggest one advantage of growing local varieties of mango trees.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
The government of Senegal plan to improve many roads that lead to the airport in the
Casamance region by 2025.
Suggest how improving roads to the airport could benefit farmers and the government.
benefit to farmers ______
benefit to the government ______

parts.label: (g)
parts.text:
Food security can be defined as:
‘when people have enough food to meet their dietary needs
for an active and healthy life.’
One farmer said,
I do not just grow and sell mango
fruits. I also grow millet and sorghum
crops and keep chickens.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Explain why this farmer is likely to have food security every year.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain ways food security could be lost.

in 2018.
The average selling price of phosphoric acid produced in Senegal was 880 USD per tonne
in 2018.
Calculate the percentage increase in value from one tonne of phosphate rock to one
tonne of phosphoric acid.
______ %

parts.text: Name two mineral ions, other than phosphate ions, that are found in fertilisers.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
Large quantities of fertiliser are used in agricultural production. Sometimes, excess
fertiliser can enter rivers and cause eutrophication.
Describe the impacts of eutrophication on aquatic ecosystems.

text: The geology of Senegal is mostly sedimentary rocks. These include large deposits of phosphate

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Gold is formed in igneous rocks. When igneous rocks are eroded, small pieces of gold are
washed away and redeposited in sedimentary rocks.
Describe the formation of igneous rock.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Many local people work in family groups to extract gold from small mines between October
and June each year.
One method of finding small pieces of gold is shown in the drawing.
water
sediment containing
gold
pan

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Describe how gold can be extracted by this method.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Another method of extracting gold is to use mercury.
Mercury is a toxic metal.
Liquid mercury is mixed with sediment. The mercury combines with the gold and the
mixture is easily removed.
The mixture of mercury and gold is then heated to make all the mercury turn to gas.
Mercury costs 14 USD per 100 grams. Gold can be sold for 30 USD per 1 gram.
Suggest reasons why people use mercury to extract gold even when they know mercury
is toxic.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
An advisor visited this mining area. The advisor explained to the miners the damage mercury
does to human health and to the local river.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Describe the environmental impacts caused by toxic substances, such as mercury,
entering a river.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The advisor gave the miners a rock-crushing machine and a table-shaker machine.
These machines can extract more gold than using mercury.
The advisor trained the miners how to use and maintain these machines.
Suggest reasons why the miners had not used these machines before.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Suggest reasons why the advisor should keep visiting these miners in the future.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text:
The mining families have been extracting gold in this region for many years.
Many miners do not have a mining licence. However, the government has no plans to
make this mining illegal.
Suggest reasons why the government does not plan to make this mining illegal.
